decks.notes: This deck focuses on using disruption, efficient removal, and countermagic to control the game and outvalue the opponent. By utilizing powerful cards like Ancestral Recall, Force of Will, and Wasteland, as well as key creatures like Lavinia, Azorius Renegade and Orcish Bowmasters, the deck aims to disrupt the opponent's game plan while building up card advantage through cards like Dig Through Time and Treasure Cruise. The inclusion of Lurrus of the Dream-Den as a companion adds even more value and flexibility to the deck's game plan.

This deck focuses on generating a high amount of mana using artifacts like Black Lotus and Moxen, combined with cards like Tolarian Academy and Paradoxical Outcome to draw through the deck and find powerful spells like Ancestral Recall and Time Walk to create overwhelming advantage. The inclusion of cards like Urza's Saga and Mishra's Bauble provide additional utility and card advantage to ensure the combo can be successfully executed. Additionally, disruption spells like Force of Will and Swords to Plowshares help protect the player's game plan while allowing them to control the tempo of the game.

The main concept of this deck is to control the game by using spells like Oath of Druids, Show and Tell, and Force of Will to disrupt the opponent's strategy while also utilizing powerful creatures like Atraxa, Grand Unifier to apply pressure. The deck also features key cards like Bolas's Citadel and Tinker to create explosive plays and win conditions. The inclusion of cards like Vexing Bauble and Gaea's Blessing allow for card advantage and deck manipulation, while the mana base with fetch lands and powerful mana artifacts allows for consistent and efficient mana production.

This deck aims to efficiently combo off using cards like Paradoxical Outcome and Moxen to generate large amounts of mana and draw cards. It includes cards like Urza's Saga and Oswald Fiddlebender to tutor for key pieces of the combo. The deck also includes disruption in the form of Force of Will and Spell Pierce to protect the combo. Lurrus of the Dream-Den is included as a companion to provide additional recursion for key cards. The deck is designed to quickly assemble its combo pieces and win the game before the opponent can effectively disrupt it.

The deck focuses on assembling the combo of Coveted Jewel and Paradoxical Outcome to generate a large amount of mana and draw cards. This allows the player to quickly find and play powerful artifacts such as The One Ring and Talon Gates of Madara. Additionally, the deck includes control elements like Force of Will and Sink into Stupor to disrupt the opponent's strategy. Overall, the strategy revolves around creating a strong board presence and overwhelming the opponent with powerful artifacts and mana production.

The deck focuses on assembling the combo of using Doomsday to stack the top of your library with specific cards, such as Thassa's Oracle, in order to win the game instantly. With a mix of tutors, cantrips, and interaction like Force of Will, the goal is to quickly and efficiently set up the Doomsday combo while protecting it from disruption. The deck aims to be versatile and adaptable, with the ability to win as early as turn one if everything falls into place.

The main goal of this Esper Control deck is to disrupt your opponent's game plan with powerful counterspells and removal spells, while also generating card advantage with card draw and selection effects like Ancestral Recall and Brainstorm. The deck aims to control the game with cards like Force of Will, Swords to Plowshares, and Spell Pierce, while also utilizing disruptive creatures like Lavinia, Azorius Renegade and Psychic Frog. The inclusion of Lurrus of the Dream-Den as a companion provides additional value by allowing you to recur cards like Mishra's Bauble and Soul-Guide Lantern from your graveyard.

The deck focuses on disrupting the opponent's strategy by playing hatebears like Thalia, Guardian of Thraben and Archon of Emeria, while also applying pressure with aggressive creatures like White Plume Adventurer. The deck also includes disruptive cards like Chalice of the Void and Strip Mine to further hinder the opponent's game plan. The use of mana acceleration like Moxen and Ancient Tomb allows the deck to quickly deploy threats and disrupt the opponent's plays, taking advantage of the Vintage format's powerful card pool to gain an edge in the matchup.

The deck revolves around using Doomsday to win the game by arranging the top five cards of the library in a specific order that will allow the player to win on their next turn. The deck includes various card draw spells, counterspells, and tutors to help set up the Doomsday combo efficiently. It also includes powerful cards like Ancestral Recall, Black Lotus, and Time Walk to help accelerate the game and gain an advantage over the opponent. The goal is to carefully plan out the sequence of cards needed to win the game quickly and efficiently.

This deck focuses on disrupting the opponent's strategy while quickly applying pressure with aggressive creatures. By playing hatebears like Archon of Emeria and Anointed Peacekeeper, it restricts the opponent's actions while creatures like White Plume Adventurer and Witch Enchanter deal damage. The deck also includes powerful mana accelerants like Ancient Tomb and Moxen to quickly deploy threats. Additionally, cards like Wasteland and Strip Mine can disrupt the opponent's mana base. The deck aims to control the game tempo and overwhelm the opponent with efficient threats and disruption.

The deck revolves around using powerful artifacts like The One Ring and Coveted Jewel, along with cards like Tinker and Paradoxical Outcome, to create a combo that generates immense value and card advantage. It also includes control elements like Force of Will and Sink into Stupor to protect the combo pieces. The deck aims to quickly assemble its key pieces using mana acceleration from cards like Mishra's Workshop and Grim Monolith, ultimately leading to a win condition through card advantage and overwhelming board presence.

This deck focuses on utilizing the powerful card Underworld Breach to create a combo that can quickly overwhelm opponents. By using cards like Brainstorm, Ponder, and Tinker to set up your plays, you can quickly chain together spells with the help of Lotus Petal and Moxen. The goal is to cast a large Brain Freeze or Bolas's Citadel to win the game, while also using Force of Will and Hullbreacher to disrupt your opponent's plays. The deck is built to be flexible and adaptable, allowing for multiple lines of play to achieve victory.

This deck focuses on using aggressive creatures with disruptive abilities to control the board and slow down the opponent's game plan. It combines hate cards like Archon of Emeria and Chancellor of the Annex with aggro creatures like Stillmoon Cavalier and White Plume Adventurer to create a disruptive and fast-paced strategy. The deck also includes mana acceleration and card draw to maintain a steady flow of threats and disruption. The goal is to quickly apply pressure while disrupting the opponent's game plan, ultimately overwhelming them with a mix of aggression and disruption.

The key strategy of this Esper Control deck is to disrupt the opponent's game plan using counter spells like Force of Will and Spell Pierce, while efficiently removing threats with Swords to Plowshares. The deck also utilizes card advantage and manipulation through cards like Ancestral Recall, Dig Through Time, and Brainstorm. Lurrus of the Dream-Den provides additional value by allowing the player to recur key cards from the graveyard. Overall, the deck aims to control the game and outvalue the opponent through efficient spell casting and resource management.

The deck focuses on utilizing graveyard recursion and synergy to quickly fill the board with powerful creatures like Stinkweed Imp, Ichorid, and Prized Amalgam. By cycling through the graveyard with cards like Golgari Thug and Golgari Grave-Troll, the deck can generate a large amount of advantage and overwhelming board presence. The deck also includes disruption elements like Force of Will and Mindbreak Trap to protect its combo pieces. The goal is to overwhelm the opponent with a fast and synergistic graveyard-based combo strategy.

The main idea of this Vintage Combo - Dredge deck is to rapidly fill up the graveyard with cards like Golgari Thug, Stinkweed Imp, and Shambling Shell, then use cards like Narcomoeba and Ichorid to bring creatures back onto the battlefield. Bazaar of Baghdad is key for card selection and graveyard filling. Prized Amalgam and Creeping Chill provide bonus value while cards like Force of Will and Force of Negation protect the combo. Grief and Hollow One offer additional disruptive threats to the opponent. Overall, the deck aims to overwhelm the opponent with graveyard recursion and powerful creatures.
